From 79bd7eab8366b29eaa099908d5694cb473684b9d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chaitanya Kulkarni <kch@nvidia.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2024 00:26:46 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] nvme-fabrics: fix I/O connect error handling

In nvmf_connect_io_queue(), if connect I/O command fails, we log the
error and continue for authentication. This overrides error captured
from __nvme_submit_sync_cmd(), causing wrong return value.

Add goto out_free_data after logging connect error to fix the issue.

Fixes: f50fff73d620c ("nvme: implement In-Band authentication")
Signed-off-by: Chaitanya Kulkarni <kch@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Hannes Reinecke <hare@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Keith Busch <kbusch@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/nvme/host/fabrics.c b/drivers/nvme/host/fabrics.c
index 3499acbf6a82..495c171daead 100644
--- a/drivers/nvme/host/fabrics.c
+++ b/drivers/nvme/host/fabrics.c
@@ -534,6 +534,7 @@ int nvmf_connect_io_queue(struct nvme_ctrl *ctrl, u16 qid)
 	if (ret) {
 		nvmf_log_connect_error(ctrl, ret, le32_to_cpu(res.u32),
 				       &cmd, data);
+		goto out_free_data;
 	}
 	result = le32_to_cpu(res.u32);
 	if (result & (NVME_CONNECT_AUTHREQ_ATR | NVME_CONNECT_AUTHREQ_ASCR)) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/nvme/host/fabrics.c`**
- In the function `nvmf_connect_io_queue`, a new line was added to handle the error case when the I/O command connection fails. Specifically, after logging the connection error with `nvmf_log_connect_error`, a `goto out_free_data;` statement was introduced. This change ensures that the function exits properly and does not continue to the authentication step if there was an error in connecting the I/O command.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification addresses a bug where the error from the I/O command connection was being overridden by the subsequent authentication process. By adding the `goto out_free_data;` statement, the flow of execution is altered to prevent further processing after an error is logged, thus preserving the integrity of the error handling and ensuring the correct return value is maintained. This change is directly related to the previous implementation of In-Band authentication, as indicated by the fix reference to commit `f50fff73d620c`.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (ret) {
    nvmf_log_connect_error(ctrl, ret, le32_to_cpu(res.u32), &cmd, data);
}
```
Reason:
When the I/O command connection fails (indicated by a non-zero `ret`), the error is logged, but the function does not exit. This allows the subsequent code related to authentication to execute, which can lead to an incorrect return value since the connection was not successfully established.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+    goto out_free_data;
```
Reason:
By adding a `goto out_free_data;` statement after logging the connection error, the function is instructed to jump to the cleanup section, effectively terminating further execution of the function. This ensures that no additional code is run after a failure, thus preserving the correct return value.
